column.text: The most important fact on the tape is that institutional money is leaving crypto, and fast. Bitcoin ETFs logged a net outflow of $299.9M on Wednesday 11 Nov, taking the seven-day total to -$1479.1M. Ether ETFs posted -$144.8M on the same day and -$556.1M over seven days. Solana ETFs added to the drain with -$10.6M on Monday 9 Nov and -$53.3M for the week. Price confirms the damage. The market has fallen 5.09% over 24 hours, and the Fear & Greed index sits at 28. Open interest is heavily skewed long, with a long/short ratio of 2.51, so retail longs are getting squeezed while top Hyperliquid accounts are leaning short. Stablecoin supply has contracted 4.83% over 30 days, which means fresh dollars are not arriving to buy the dip. Dollar liquidity is tightening, and risk assets are running into that headwind. The bounce case is real but thin. Daily RSI on BTC and ETH is below 30, and the temptation is to call a bottom. Oversold alone is not a mechanism. Without buying volume behind it, a bounce is a place to sell. Desk stance: stay with continuation shorts while the trend holds, and treat failed rallies as the better-odds short. Longs need a genuine trigger, such as deeply negative funding, a capitulation reading, a real demand catalyst, or a failed breakdown. Until one of those shows up, the trend is the trade. Watch for ETF flows to turn positive and stablecoin supply to stop shrinking. Until both happen, sellers keep control.
